Welcome to CSCU9M3: Scripting for Data Science

Learn how to represent, manipulate, analyse and present data using Python—progressing from core programming foundations to data science applications including natural language processing and computer vision.

ABOUT THIS MODULE SYLLABUS MODULES ASSIGNMENTS

What you will study

You'll start by learning the basics of Python programming and then move on to more advanced topics such as natural language processing and computer vision, where you will practise the concepts that you have learned in Python.

Essential software and module notes

  • We will use the Python data science software environment Anaconda, which you can download and install for free.
  • Detailed module notes are available here: Scripting4DS-1.pdf.

About the videos: Some videos were originally produced for a Stirling module called Representing and Manipulating Data. They are the correct videos for this module. Some feature staff who are not teaching CSCU9M3, so please direct questions to the staff listed below.

Your module staff

Dr. Donie Jardeleza, FHEA (British University Vietnam)
Burcu Can Buglalilar, Module Coordinator (University of Stirling)
Leonardo Bezerra (University of Stirling)

Learning outcomes

On successful completion of this module, you should be able to:

  1. Write short Python programs to load, store, manipulate, analyse, present and save data from a variety of sources.
  2. Choose appropriate Python libraries for different tasks.
  3. Choose appropriate representations for data from different sources.
  4. Manage the storage, retrieval and sharing of large data sets online.
  5. Choose an appropriate scripting tool for a given task.

Start here

  1. Read About this module.
  2. Check the Syllabus for key dates and the module outline.
  3. Open Modules for weekly information and all learning content.
  4. Begin with Week 0 – Read Me First, then work through the weekly content in order.

Find support

Time at university can be exciting, but it can also feel stressful or overwhelming at times. If at any point during the year you feel like you’re struggling or need support, please remember you are not alone. We are here to help.

Please contact your Module Coordinator through the Key Contacts page or speak with your Personal Tutor.

You can also visit Key Support Routes, including the University's Student Learning Services and Mental Health and Wellbeing Service.
